title: Hawker Centre & Kopitiam
description: Order your kopi and makan like a local — in Mandarin.

items.note: "Kopitiam" is Hokkien for 咖啡店 — the neighbourhood coffee shop with drink stall and food stalls.

example.zh: 我们 在 楼下 的 咖啡店 见。
example.en: Let's meet at the coffee shop downstairs.

example.zh: 我 每天 早上 喝 咖啡。

items.note: 乌 (wū, black) is the "O" in kopi-O, from Hokkien. Kopi-O kosong = no sugar.

example.zh: 老板， 一杯 咖啡乌。
我 要 一杯 热 茶。
example.en: I'd like a cup of hot tea.

items.note: The Chinese name for the Milo drink used in Singapore and Malaysia.

example.zh: 小孩 都 喜欢 喝 美禄。

items.note: "Peng" in kopi-peng is the Hokkien way of saying 冰.

example.zh: 咖啡乌 加 冰。
一杯 茶， 少糖。

items.note: "Tapau" / "da bao" — Singaporeans use this for takeaway. Elsewhere it often means packing up leftovers.

example.zh: 两份 鸡饭， 打包。
在 这里 吃 还是 打包？
一杯 咖啡乌， 一杯 茶。
我 要 一碗 云吞面。
example.en: I want a bowl of wanton mee.

items.english: boss (what you call the stall owner)
items.note: Singaporeans call any hawker 老板 — or Uncle / Auntie.

example.zh: 老板， 多少钱？

items.note: Singapore's hawker culture was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2020.

example.zh: 这个 小贩中心 很 热闹。
example.en: This hawker centre is very lively.

items.note: Full name: 海南鸡饭 (Hǎinán jī fàn), Hainanese chicken rice.

example.zh: 这 家 鸡饭 很 有名。
example.en: This chicken rice stall is famous.

items.note: 粿条 (kway teow) is the flat rice noodle; 炒 means stir-fried.

example.zh: 炒粿条 不 要 太 辣。
example.en: Char kway teow, not too spicy.

items.note: From Malay "laksa". 叻 is the same character as in 石叻 — an old name for Singapore.

example.zh: 我 最 喜欢 吃 叻沙。
我们 叫 二十 支 沙爹。
example.en: Let's order twenty sticks of satay.

items.note: 云吞 is the Cantonese-style word for wonton.

example.zh: 云吞面 要 加 辣椒 吗？
example.en: Want chilli with your wanton mee?

items.note: Hokkien for "meat bone tea". There's no tea in it — it's a peppery pork rib soup.

example.zh: 下雨天 最 适合 喝 肉骨茶。
example.en: Rainy days are perfect for bak kut teh.

example.zh: 早餐 吃 椰浆饭。

items.note: From Malay "rojak" — also slang for anything mixed-up, like "rojak" language.

example.zh: 罗惹 又 甜 又 香。

items.note: Also called 杂菜饭 (zá cài fàn). Pick your dishes, pay by what's on the plate.

example.zh: 经济饭 一 菜 一 肉 多少钱？
example.en: How much is economy rice with one veg and one meat?

example.zh: 天气 好 热， 来 一碗 红豆冰 吧。
example.en: It's so hot — let's have an ice kacang.

items.note: From Malay "kaya". 半生熟蛋 (bàn shēng shú dàn) are the soft-boiled eggs that come with kaya toast.

example.zh: 咖椰 吐司 配 半生熟蛋。
这个 辣 不 辣？
辣椒 自己 拿。
这个 叻沙 很 好吃！
我 饿 了， 去 吃饭 吧。
我 吃 饱 了。
一碗 面， 不要辣。
example.en: One bowl of noodles, no chilli.

items.note: The famous Singaporean habit of reserving a table with a tissue packet.

example.zh: 我 先 去 霸位。
example.en: I'll go chope a seat first.

example.zh: 那 家 要 排队 很 久。
example.en: You have to queue a long time at that stall.

example.zh: 这个 摊位 只 开 早上。
example.en: This stall only opens in the morning.

example.zh: 用 纸巾 霸位。
example.en: Chope a seat with a tissue packet.

example.zh: 今天 叫 外卖 吧。
吃 完 请 归还 托盘。
example.en: Please return your tray after eating.
